d1.text: The amendment would relocate the marine terminal berth 180 metres north of the location assessed in 2022, reducing dredging volumes and the area of seabed disturbed.
Sediment control measures during construction follow the erosion and sediment control plan approved under Condition 12, with monitoring at the laydown area and the outfall.
Caribou habitat in the transmission corridor is unaffected by the amendment; no new clearing is proposed outside the existing right of way.

d2.text: The proponent must describe the effects of the amended terminal design on marine water quality, including turbidity from dredging and sediment deposition rates.
Engagement with participating Indigenous nations must address harvesting in the affected marine area and the timing of in-water works.

d3.text: One advisory was issued regarding sediment control at the marine terminal laydown area. The proponent had installed silt fencing but had not maintained it after the January rainfall.

d5.text: Annual sediment monitoring results remained below the trigger values in the certificate for all twelve sampling stations.
Caribou monitoring was carried out in partnership with the nation’s guardians programme; no calving activity was recorded within the project footprint.

d8.text: This certificate is issued under section 29 of the Environmental Assessment Act, 2018, subject to the 38 conditions in Schedule B.
Condition 12 requires an erosion and sediment control plan, prepared by a qualified professional and updated before each construction season.

d10.text: The assessment concludes that residual effects on marine water quality are not significant, given the sediment control measures required by the conditions.
Effects on caribou were assessed as significant and adverse before mitigation, and not significant after the habitat offset required by Condition 21.

d12.text: Forty-one submissions raised sediment and water quality; the assessment team’s response is in Appendix C.

d13.text: Dredging is scheduled outside the marine fish window. Sediment plumes are modelled to dissipate within 400 metres of the dredge head.
